As always, thanks for reading! 歡迎來到台灣 Coming to you this week from the chilled spa town of Jiaoxi, Taiwan (around 1.5 hours on the train outside the capital Taipei) where I’m spending a few days soaking in the vibe en route to Europe (avoiding the Gulf!) (Hence a few hours behind on clicking “send” due to timezone difference…) First time I’ve visited Taiwan, a few travel notes: Very first impression: my airport Uber driver(!) and I had a long conversation (mediated by ChatGPT voice translation) - discussing the differences between TSMC’s various 2/3...28nm chip fabrication processes and export markets. TSMC clearly dominates the country’s export economy and is a source of national pride... I enjoyed a catchup with the team at MIC, Taiwan’s leading tech policy thinktank , comparing notes on small advanced economy AI sovereignty and strategies —Taiwan has been very progressive over the last decade with the work of Audrey Tang in particular. Like Aotearoa, it also has a significant indigenous population seeking to ensure AI aligns with their own cultural inheritance. However *unlike Aotearoa*, Taiwan has a uniquely pivotal position in the global AI supply chain currently… which has all sorts of benefits / strategic complications… Without exception, everyone is very polite and helpful… and the country feels really safe, even in the denser parts of Taipei. Street food plentiful and very affordable compared to AoNZ. Streets are bustling with people, cars and mopeds (although nothing like Vietnam!) Air quality is ok but lots of petrol fumes near busy roads. No jaywalking and everyone waits patiently for the pedestrian crossing light to turn green. The language barrier is a challenge even with AI to help out — most of the time I’m pretty much the only Westerner wandering around the city - luckily people speak some English but I really need to invest time in getting skilled up with more than just “Xiexie” (thank you)… Mobile / internet connectivity everywhere I’ve been has been super reliable (roaming on 2Degrees SIM, just NZ$8/day all in - I could get an eSIM for less, no doubt, if I was here longer) The landmark Taipei 101 is *really tall*… (up in the clouds the day I visited!) The day starts late and goes on long into the night (night markets are plentiful throughout Taipei)… as a result my 7am cafe rhythm has struggled, particularly adjusting from AoNZ timezone.
